purpose: Provide one stable upstream dependency surface for P-number invocation so downstream repositories and agents can resolve and execute prompts without understanding Prompt Kit registry layout, migration topology, retained donor repositories, or conversational/model memory.

ownership_boundary.downstream_rule: Downstream repositories consume this contract and do not reimplement prompt discovery, registry composition, retained-source routing, or authority selection.
ownership_boundary.upstream_rule: The upstream resolver owns registry composition, authority routing, migration compatibility, and distribution catalog generation.
ownership_boundary.retained_authority_rule: Retained repository-local prompts may be distributed through the upstream catalog without transferring prompt-definition authority.
ownership_boundary.rename_rule: Repository slug and physical source paths are provenance, not semantic API identity. Consumers bind to contract_id/schema_version and a configurable upstream locator.

live_upstream.description: Resolver runs in an upstream environment with current canonical sources.

pinned_catalog.description: Resolver consumes the tracked upstream catalog. Exact source provenance is preserved, but freshness is bounded by the catalog build inputs.

invariants: Exact P-number identity wins; fuzzy semantic substitution is forbidden.
An invoked operational prompt is instructions to execute, not text to rewrite.
invoke and implement requires both execution and implementation intent in the result packet.
Downstream consumers never need a Triage checkout or Prompt Kit registry topology.
The distribution catalog is generated and provenance-preserving, never a competing prompt-definition authority.
Unknown or conflicting authority fails closed instead of guessing.
Prompt contribution, mutation, retirement, and registry governance remain upstream-owner concerns, not downstream consumer concerns.
proof_ceiling: This contract proves deterministic prompt identity/intent resolution and provenance. Actual prompt execution, repository mutation, validation, integration, deployment, and production behavior remain separate proof states.
